### Funnel chart
Steps people take in order, each drawn as a stage as wide as the people who reach it.

Component ID: `funnel-chart`

[Component documentation](https://www.expressivecss.com/funnel-chart.html.md) · [Repository source](https://github.com/BaezFJ/ExpressiveCSS/blob/master/docs/src/pages/funnel-chart.astro) · [Matching tag](https://github.com/BaezFJ/ExpressiveCSS/tree/v0.15.0)

#### Selection and adaptation

Runtime ownership: `auto-init`. No dedicated entry in the reviewed Google component inventory.

Example: Visits, signups, trials and paid accounts this month is a funnel chart. Signups by channel is a bar chart.

#### Material mapping

Relationship: none. Web extension; no dedicated entry was observed in the reviewed current M3 component inventory.

Upstream: web-extension-inventory-reviewed (2026-10-25); [evidence](https://m3.material.io/components).

Requirements and boundaries: design reference web-extensions-review. The inventory page renders client-side, so this review relies on the 2026-09-13 inventory review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.

Support (2026-10-25, `llm.md#funnel-chart`): Stages drawn from a figure's data table, one per row from the second column in table order, centered and as wide as their value against the largest, gaps and values of zero or less left without a stage, row labels at the inline start, a pointer and keyboard tooltip that adds each stage's percentage of the first row, update() width motion and data-watch.

Web adaptation: The <table> stays in the page as the text alternative and the no-JavaScript fallback; the stages are aria-hidden and the plot is one Tab stop with a polite live tooltip.

Known boundary: Stage widths and order in left-to-right and right-to-left pages, gaps, labels, the tooltip and its percentages, keyboard steps, the pointer, update() motion and data-watch are checked in a browser; screen reader output, forced colors and enlarged text remain unverified. There are no tapered stages, colors per row, step-to-step conversion rates or horizontal funnels.

Full parity remains unassessed. [Capability evidence](../references/capability-roadmap.md#funnel-chart).

#### Contract

A `<figure class="funnel-chart">` takes a `<figcaption>` and a `<table>`. The first column labels each row and the second holds its value. `AutoInit()` draws each row as a stage, from the top down in table order, centered and as wide as its value against the largest one, which fills the chart. Each row's label sits beside its stage at the inline start. The table stays in the page, visually hidden, as the chart's text alternative; without JavaScript it shows instead of the chart.

#### Syntax

```html
<figure class="funnel-chart">
  <figcaption>Signups this month</figcaption>
  <table>
    <thead>
      <tr><th>Step</th><th>People</th><th>Revenue</th></tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr><th>Visited</th><td>12,000</td><td>$0</td></tr>
      <tr><th>Signed up</th><td>4,800</td><td>$0</td></tr>
      <tr><th>Paid</th><td>640</td><td>$19,200</td></tr>
    </tbody>
  </table>
</figure>
```

#### Also documented

The Funnel chart section of the [API reference](https://www.expressivecss.com/llm.md) also covers Tokens.

#### Rules

- `funnel-chart-is-a-figure-with-a-table`: Write .funnel-chart as a <figure> holding a <table> of the data. The drawn chart is hidden from assistive technology, so the table is all a screen reader reads, and it is what shows without JavaScript.
- `funnel-chart-has-a-caption`: Name a .funnel-chart with a <figcaption>. It names the focusable plot as well as the figure; hide it with .visually-hidden when nearby text already names the chart.
